title.en: The writer, the travellers and the goal

heading.en: A road to a sacred mountain

hook.en: Imagine driving for days across an empty, freezing plateau where the air is so thin that even sleeping is hard. Nick Middleton made such a journey to walk around one of Asia's holiest mountains.

objectives.en: Identify the author and the form of the text (travel writing)
Name the narrator's companions, Tsetan and Norbu
State the purpose of the journey: the kora around Mount Kailash

narration.en: Imagine driving for days across an empty, freezing plateau where the air is so thin that even sleeping is hard. Nick Middleton made such a journey to walk around one of Asia's holiest mountains.

body.en: Nick Middleton is a British geographer and travel writer, and "Silk Road" is a first-person account of one of his journeys. He travels from Ravu across western Tibet towards Mount Kailash. His goal is the kora, the pilgrims' walk around the sacred mountain.

points.en: Genre: travelogue (travel writing), told in the first person
Setting: the high plateau of western Tibet
Destination: Mount Kailash, holy to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and followers of Bon
Kora: a ritual walk (circumambulation) around a sacred place

narration.en: Nick Middleton is a British geographer and travel writer, and "Silk Road" is a first-person account of one of his journeys. He travels from Ravu across western Tibet towards Mount Kailash. His goal is the kora, the pilgrims' walk around the sacred mountain.
Let us map the people of this travelogue around the narrator before we follow the route.

say.en: At the centre of the story is the narrator, Nick Middleton, a travel writer who tells everything in the first person.
Tsetan is the driver. He is calm and expert, and he finds short cuts across the plateau.
Norbu is a Tibetan scholar from Lhasa who goes with the writer towards Kailash.
The goal of the journey is Mount Kailash, where pilgrims walk the kora around the mountain.
On the way the travellers meet nomad herders and their fierce guard dogs.

problem.en: What was the purpose of the narrator's journey in "Silk Road"?

steps.en: Name the destination: Mount Kailash in western Tibet.
Name the aim: to complete the kora, the sacred walk around the mountain.
Add context: the mountain is holy to several faiths, so pilgrims make this circuit.

answer.en: The narrator travelled across western Tibet to reach Mount Kailash and complete the kora, the pilgrims' sacred walk around the mountain, which is holy to several faiths, observing the land and its people on the way.
